beats.narration: That ticking sound when you start your car cold?
beats.visualPrompt: Static exterior shot of a car on a cold morning, visible exhaust vapor condensing from the tailpipe against frosty air, frost lightly dusting the windshield, engine idling, low winter sun.

beats.narration: Loudest right after startup. Quiets down in a minute or two.
beats.visualPrompt: Low-angle under-hood shot of an idling engine bay, camera holding steady as subtle heat-shimmer builds near the exhaust manifold over the shot.
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two ~2.5s sub-shots before real generation to satisfy the 1.5-2.5s visual-change cadence.

beats.narration: One clue: a small exhaust manifold leak. Metal contracts when cold, so the gap ticks until it seals up warm.
beats.visualPrompt: Macro/cutaway shot: an exhaust manifold flange with a visible thin carbon-soot streak trailing from the gasket seam, slow push-in revealing the leak path.
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two sub-shots (wide + macro push-in) before real generation.

beats.narration: That gap can also let exhaust gas — including carbon monoxide — into the engine bay.
beats.visualPrompt: A fixture-mounted combustion/CO leak detector wand held near the manifold gap, small indicator light activating, dim shop-bay lighting, no hand in frame.

beats.narration: Don't ignore a cold-start tick. A quick listen can confirm where it's coming from.
beats.visualPrompt: A mechanic's stethoscope-style listening probe clipped against an engine component, tool visible, no hand or arm in frame, a simple audio-waveform graphic overlay pulsing in sync with engine idle.
beats.renderIntegrityNote: Split into two sub-shots before real generation.

beats.narration: Worth checking before it gets worse. Stop by and we'll take a look — Nick's Tire & Auto.
